title: GitHub Trending Today #56: learnharness, tstack, iFixAi, hallmark, project-maya, neuron-explorer

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Welcome back to GitHub awesome. This is GitHub trending today number 56. 35 trending open source projects on GitHub right now. Let's get into it.

sections.title: learnharness
paragraphs: Learn Harness is a desktop app where AI agents help you learn something difficult. First, it measures what you already understand. Then, it plans a path to your goal and teaches you step by step with practice sessions later on. As you work, you can think out loud and explain your reasoning in your own words. Everything you learn goes into a knowledge graph that carries over between sessions.

sections.title: tstack
paragraphs: Tstack is Theo's collection of the agent skills he uses every day in Claude code and codecs cleaned up so anyone can use them. Say full send and an agent takes a change all the way through. It proves the change works, gets it reviewed, files the PR, watches CI and merges. Council gets a second opinion on your changes from models made by other providers.

sections.title: iFixAi
paragraphs: IFIXA is an open-source Python tool for auditing AI agents before they go live. It builds a simulated business around your agent, like a fintech support desk, then sends it realistic requests, including ones that push it past its role. A judge model grades every reply, and the agent gets an A tof score across five areas. fail one of the three must pass checks and the grade is capped at D.

sections.title: hallmark
paragraphs: Hallmark gives coding agents a design workflow for escaping the same generic landing page. It offers visual themes or a custom direction, builds around the visitors actual task, then checks the result in a browser for layout problems and repetitive design habits. It can also audit or redesign existing pages while checking that links and forms survive. Full visual checks require Chrome and Puppeteer.

sections.title: project-maya
paragraphs: Project Maya runs large mixture of experts models locally by keeping frequently used experts on your GPU and moving the rest between RAM and SSD. It includes browser chat, a live hardware monitor, and compatible APIs for connecting coding agents. Setup measures your hardware and tunes the engine around it. Model files are substantial. Performance depends on your memory and storage.

sections.title: ex-ussr-kinship-research
paragraphs: ExusR kinship research is a genealogy skill for agents like Claude Code and Codeex built for tracing family history through records from the former USSR and the Russian Empire. The agent sets up a case folder and works through church civil military deportation and repression records. Every source gets saved with a hash and every claim is logged as single source or corroborated.

sections.title: neuron-explorer
paragraphs: Neuron Explorer is an interpretability tool for the Quen 354B model that works by steering. For every neuron in a layer, it pushes that neuron up and down on a few prompts and keeps every resulting output. Then it lays the neurons out on a 3D map of the model. It ranks them by which word clusters they push the text toward measured against random controls.

sections.title: ascii-reveal
paragraphs: Aski Reveal makes text, images, and entire cards decode into place through a wave of scrambled characters. Wrap your React content, connect its loading state, and pair it with asy skeletons while data arrives. The effect draws above the real content, keeping layout stable and text available to screen readers. Reduced motion settings get a short fade, and slower devices automatically fall back to one. Two.

sections.title: minilytics
paragraphs: Minolytics is self-hosted web analytics that puts revenue first, running on Cloudflare workers with a D1 database and a React dashboard. A small script on your site records page views, clicks, and goals. When someone pays, a payment web hook credits the sale to the last source that sent that visitor. sections.title: AARE
paragraphs: is an open-source rebuild of the phone side of Android Auto, so your phone can talk to your car's screen without Google Play services. It speaks the Android Auto protocol to the car's head unit, draws the car display, and runs apps Google's version doesn't allow, like the COM apps navigation app or signal. It handles media, messages through notifications, navigation on the driver's cluster, and a voice assistant.

sections.title: BeautifulRust
paragraphs: Beautiful Rust is a Claude code plugin with a single skill that teaches Claude to write clean, idiomatic Rust. It distills five well-known guides, including Google's Rust style guide, the official Rust API guidelines, and Microsoft's pragmatic Rust guidelines. It covers ownership, API design, error handling, concurrency, and unsafe code, and it loads on its own whenever you're working in Rust.

sections.title: dimensional-drawing
paragraphs: Dimensional drawing is a set of agent skills that turns any UI component into a one-page technical drawing in the style of Apple's published dimensional drawings. Point your agent at a component file, a storybook story, a URL, or a screenshot. It draws a sheet with a plan view, exploded layers, detail views, and tables of every padding, gap, and corner radius.

sections.title: keybytes
paragraphs: Keyes is an open- source modular keyboard where every single key is its own little circuit board. You can rearrange each key called a key bit has a Cherry MX switch and a tiny Risk V chip. Pogo pins on all four sides carry power and data so the keys snap together and onto a mainboard with Bluetooth and USBC. The mainboard even programs each key through those same pins. The cases are magnetic.

sections.title: webframe
paragraphs: Web frame is a go command line tool that runs a web page like a program. It loads a URL or a local file in a hidden web view, sends the pages console logs to standard output and its errors to standard error. It can even run JavaScript you pipe in. It uses your systems own web view like WebKit on Mac OS or Webview 2 on Windows, so there's no bundled browser and the binary stays small.

sections.title: raven
paragraphs: Raven runs Windows applications on Linux with no virtual machine and no wine style tweaking. You install a program with its own normal installer and it just starts. The program's code runs directly on your CPU inside a sandbox while Raven answers every system call by playing the part of the Windows kernel from files and the registry to Windows and input.

sections.title: pngdeer
paragraphs: PNG is a lossy PNG compressor with no quality slider written in Rust and compiled to web assembly. So it also runs in your browser. Instead of making you pick a setting, it tries pallet sizes from two up to 256 colors with and without dithering. Each result gets scored with a perceptual metric and it keeps the smallest file that still looks right. It works from the command line on Mac OS and Linux or in the browser.

sections.title: lantern
paragraphs: Lantern is a TypeScript library for making animated step-by-step explainers of code changes and it runs in the browser on Cloudflare workers or in Node. It ports the core of Manom, the Python animation engine behind three blue one browns videos to JavaScript with no dependencies and draws everything as SVG. Every scene runs on a fixed clock, so jumping to any moment always looks the same.

sections.title: gdirect
paragraphs: GDirect is a Rust tool for using Google Drive entirely from the terminal. You can browse your files interactively, download and upload, and export Google Docs as PDFs. Downloads run through Arya 2 with several connections at once, so they're fast, they resume after an interruption, and they get checked against MD5 hashes. You can also mount your drive as a folder on Mac OS or Linux.

sections.title: whatsmyagentdoing
paragraphs: What's my agent doing is a local dashboard that shows what all your Claude code, codecs, and Gemini CLI agents are up to, built on Node with no dependencies. Type slashmy office and your agents show up as little workers in an isometric office in 2D or 3D or as a plain list. Each one's status changes live from thinking and running to waiting for you, done or stuck on an error. Reader is a clawed code skill

sections.title: rederive
paragraphs: that teaches you a codebase by making you rediscover its design decisions yourself. Instead of explaining anything, it only asks guiding questions. A background agent reads the code, the links between files, and the commit history, then builds a map of 5 to 10 problems the original authors had to solve. Get stuck and the hints narrow down.

sections.title: esp-labs-web
paragraphs: S Peach Labs-Web is a bench guide for learning the ESP32S3 microcontroller built as a React app. It shows a live pin out of the board and walks you through lessons for each track, each with its own simulator and diagrams. A built-in code reader lets you tour and explore the companion firmware with several views of the same code. You can set your level, how many hints you want, and how much motion the interface uses.

sections.title: farol
paragraphs: For all shows where a pull request deserves your attention by tracing changed code to the pages, endpoints, and jobs it affects. It ranks risky files, flags contract changes, and brings existing coverage and lint reports into the review. Run it locally or through GitHub actions for TypeScript, Go, and Python projects. It scores guide review effort. Code it can't understand gets marked unknown and sent for closer inspection.

sections.title: LinuxRunner
paragraphs: Linux Runner runs real ARM 64 Linux apps and even full desktops on an iPhone built on ISH. It doesn't boot a Linux kernel or run a virtual machine. Instead, it interprets the app's instructions and answers each Linux system call itself with no jailbreak and no JIT. You pick a Debian or Alpine environment and get a terminal, a desktop or experimental KDE plasma.

sections.title: correlation
paragraphs: Correlation is a research project that asks a simple question. Can stock correlations predict the market? It crunches lagged correlations across about 13,000 US stocks and funds with a Rust engine running on the GPU and a desktop app to explore the results. Every strategy gets tested on held out data with a $10,000 account and compared against random accounts that trade just as often.

sections.title: unbloat-android-tv
paragraphs: Unbloat Android TV slims down an Android TV from a Windows PC. Then installs Zenhome, a minimal Apple TV style home screen. A script connects to the TV over your network with ADB. It backs up your apps and settings first, then switches off ads, telemetry, and unneeded services from brand specific lists for TCL, Sony, Philips, Xiaomi, and others.

sections.title: enzyme
paragraphs: Enzyme is a compile step for your notes that helps AI agents find their way around a knowledge base. pointed at a folder of markdown like an Obsidian vault or a Readwise export and it builds a concept graph from your tags, links, folders, and dates. It also writes a set of thematic questions ahead of time so your agent can search those instead of gpping through raw files.

sections.title: studyai
paragraphs: Study AI is a local study app for university lectures built with React and TypeScript. Import your PowerPoint slides and it pulls out the text, tables, charts, speaker notes, and even equations, then shows them next to each slide. You study with spaced repetition, flashcards, notes, and practice exams, and all your lecture data stays in your browser. An optional AI tutor runs on a Cloudflare worker you deploy yourself.

sections.title: openidea
paragraphs: Open IDA is a desktop IDE rebuilt in Rust for developers who like Intelligj's keymap and workflow, but want something lighter. It runs as a native app through Tari on Mac OS, Windows, and Linux. It comes with an editor, code insight, a debugger, git, a terminal, and database, and HTTP clients covering more than 60 languages through language servers.

sections.title: omarchytv
paragraphs: Omari TV is an unofficial Android TV home screen styled after the Omari Linux desktop. It replaces the stock launcher with five workspaces for home, TV inputs, all your apps, a PC link, and system settings. It comes with 26 themes in 4K and 37 ASI art screen savers. A plugin for your PC or Mac pairs with the TV to sync themes and mirror your screen.

sections.title: SuperGhidra

sections.title: hob
paragraphs: running AI models on your own computer built on Electron and Llama.cpp. It checks your machine and picks the best openweight model that fits like Gemma or GPTOSS, then sets everything up for you. It runs on Mac, Windows, and Linux with 8 GB of memory or more. You can have it fill out PDFs, work through analyze a spreadsheet, and draw a chart.

sections.title: tellyscope
paragraphs: Telescope is Android app that manages your Android TV, Google TV, or Fire TV right in Cotlin. It connects over your network with ADB and debloat the TV using lists made for each model. Apps get disabled, never uninstalled, and a protected list keeps critical system apps safe. You can also install apps, move files back and forth, and tweak settings like private DNS.

sections.title: all-historical-evidence-of-jesus-christ
paragraphs: This project is a searchable archive of the historical sources about Jesus of Nazareth. from New Testament and non-cononical gospels to Roman documents and archaeology built as a static site with Python tools. The tools pull every reference out of a research dossier and mirror the source texts. Then they link a citation to a document only when that document actually contains the quoted passage.
